To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dyes containing the cyano-ester functionalization on the squarate core show the highest performance, in terms of short-circuit current density (Jsc), open-circuit potential (Voc), fill factor (FF) and overall energy conversion efficiency (η) in DSSCs.
the introduction of cyano-ester groups on the squarate core unit of the benzoindolenie squaraine dye leads to a significant increase of the molar absorption coefficient in the NIR region.

the introduction of cyano-ester groups into the central squaric core of the dyes leads to a significant enhancement of the photovoltaic performance of the DSSCs, with respect to the dyes containing the dicyanomethylene moiety.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel centrally functionalised symmetric benzoindolene squaraine dye sensitizers for DSCs.
the synthesis and characterization of a series of novel centrally functionalised squaraines.
the design and synthesis of novel centrally functionalised symmetric benzoindole-nine squaraine (BISQ) dyes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of the dicyanobenzoindolenine dye, the extension of the conjugation length of the π-electronic system leads to an increase in the light harvesting efficiency and to an improvement in the charge separation efficiency.

the cyano-ester functionalized benzoindolenines show a better photovoltaic performance in comparison with the dicyanvinyl analogs, due to the higher absorption coefficient in the NIR region and the higher molar extinction coefficient in the visible region.
the dicyanomethyl group is the best functionalization for the squaric acid core, while the cyano-ester is a good choice for the benzoindolenium moiety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dyes with a dicyanovinyloxy substitution in the core unit show a better performance in DSSCs than the dyes with the cyano-ester substitution in the core.

the dicyanobenzene substituted squaraine dye 3a showed the best photovoltaic performance with a short circuit current density of 5.3 mA/cm2, an open circuit voltage of 0.63 V and a fill factor of 0.55.

the introduction of the cyano-ester functional group in the central part of the squaraine dicyanovinylic dye is a good approach for the design of new panchromatic dyes for the development of efficient dye-sensitized solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the central functionalization has a significant effect on the photoelectrical properties of the dyes and on the photovoltaic performance of the dye-sensitized solar cells.
the central functionalization of squaraine dices has a great influence on the dye-sensitized solar cell performance.
the cyano-ester substituted benzoindolenines show a better performance in DSSCs, in particular, when the cyano-esters are extended with an alkyl chain of 4 carbon atoms (4CE).
